title: Large Language Models Reflect Human Citation Patterns with a Heightened Citation Bias

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs to suggest scholarly references for anonymized in-text citations and comparing the historical citation counts of the generated references against the ground truth references using the Semantic Scholar database.

Comparing the distribution of publication venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICLR, AAAI, arXiv) of LLM-generated references to the ground truth references to see if models disproportionately favor specific high-profile venues.
Analyzing and comparing the temporal distribution (publication years) of LLM-generated references against ground truth citations to measure preferences for recent versus older publications.
Measuring and comparing the number of characters in the titles of LLM-generated references versus the ground truth to identify preferences for shorter or longer titles.
Comparing the distribution of the number of authors in LLM-generated references against the ground truth to observe preferences for papers with solo, small, or large author groups.
